payload_summary:
CW-20260508-0010: chose Option B (prune nanite wiring only; keep adapters in go-providers). Cross-portfolio scan found agent-mux + clockwork-manifold consume New{Aider,Copilot,Gemini,Junie,Kiro,Qwen}Adapter directly — Option A would silently break two parallel consumers.</payload_summary>
<parameter name="payload_body">## Decision

For CW-20260508-0010 (prune unused CLI adapters from nanite), the implementer prompt offered Option A (delete the six adapters from go-providers) vs Option B (keep them in go-providers, only prune nanite wiring) gated on a cross-portfolio consumer scan.

**Verdict: Option B.** The grep returned non-zero matches:

- `agent-mux/internal/app/service.go:590-600` — `gop.New{Aider,Copilot,Gemini,Junie,Kiro,Qwen}Adapter()` (all six, in a switch).
- `clockwork-manifold/internal/runtime/agent/factory.go:75,82` — `provider.NewGeminiAdapter()`, `provider.NewCopilotAdapter()`.
- `clockwork-manifold/internal/runtime/agent/bootdir_test.go:139,154` — same two in tests.

Deleting from go-providers would have broken two parallel portfolio consumers immediately, with no advance coordination.

## What was done

Branch: `feat/cw-20260508-0010-prune-cli-adapters` (worktree: `~/Projects-apps/nanite-cw-0010-cli-prune`).
Final commit: `c6f9376`.
Touched (nanite only):
- `cmd/nanite/main.go`: dropped six `provider.New<X>Adapter()` calls from the `cliAdapters` slice in `initProviders`. Migrated aliased symbols per Wave-2 Path B (`provider.Provider` → `llmcontracts.Provider` x14, `provider.ToolDefinition` → `llmtypes.ToolDefinition` x1) with new imports.
- `internal/api/provider_manage.go::handleDetectCLI`: trimmed the parallel auto-detection list to claude/codex/opencode (extra-scope but same-spirit; otherwise the `/detect-cli` HTTP endpoint surfaces dead detection results to the UI). Side note: the original list was missing opencode entirely — added it so the API matches main.go's actual production set.

Did not touch:
- `internal/service/container.go` fallback list — already claude/codex/opencode only.
- `~/Projects-apps/go-providers/provider/pty_{gemini,copilot,aider,junie,kiro,qwen}.go` — adapters stay.

## Why Option B over Option A

1. **Cross-portfolio breakage.** Option A breaks agent-mux and clockwork-manifold in the same sprint window. Without surfacing it as a fold-in question, that's silent collateral.
2. **Asymmetric risk.** Option B costs ~10 lines of dead-code carrying in go-providers. Option A costs two consumer repos going red mid-sprint with no coordinator.
3. **Future-resurrect optionality.** If a future production consumer wants gemini/copilot/etc as a CLI again, the adapter is there. If it's deleted, the resurrection cost is non-trivial because the test fixtures and Detect() shape go with it.

## Decisions locked

- Production CLI shapes are claude / codex / opencode. Anything else is dead in nanite.
- The nanite `/detect-cli` endpoint mirrors the production cliAdapters slice.
- `provider.Provider` and `provider.ToolDefinition` migrated to their new homes per Path B (touched files only).

## Follow-up candidates

- `internal/store/seed.go` and `pkg/models/registry.go` still seed DB rows / model entries for `pty-{copilot,aider,junie,kiro,qwen}-001` and corresponding model IDs. They will never resolve at runtime (no adapter is registered to dispatch on them). A separate ticket should either drop the seed entries + write a migration to clean existing rows, or leave them as inert data. Lowest-cost option: leave them; the user-facing UI lists are filtered by `Has(providerType)` registration anyway.
- If agent-mux and clockwork-manifold ever prune the six adapters in their own cleanup passes, Option A becomes viable for go-providers (no consumers anywhere). Track as a `feedback_no_compat_shims`-flavored followup.
- Branch name normalization: orchestrator created `feat/...` but the prompt specified `chore/...`. Standardize at orchestrator level for cleanup tickets.

## Out of scope (deliberate)

- `cmd/nanite/main.go::initProviders` apiProviders block (lines 480-509) — references Wave-1-deleted symbols (`provider.NewAnthropic`, `provider.NewOpenAI`, `provider.NewGemini`, `provider.NewMistral`, `provider.NewOpenRouter`, `provider.NewOpenZen`, `provider.NewAzureOpenAI`, `provider.NewOllama` plus type assertions). Owned by sibling tickets CW-20260508-0011 (Anthropic SDK wrapper), CW-20260508-0012 (OpenAI SDK wrapper). Other vendors out of release scope.
- HTTP API provider deletions in go-providers — CW-20260508-0013.
- Reintroducing pruned adapters as SDK wrappers — post-release scope.

## Verification state at handoff

- `go vet ./...`: fails with one error — `internal/context/overflow.go:97:29: undefined: provider.ErrRequestExceedsRateBudget`. **Pre-existing baseline error** from Wave-1 deletions; owned by CW-0011's migration. Confirmed pre-existing via `git stash && go vet`. My changes introduce zero new vet errors.
- `go test ./... -race`: same root-cause build failure; cannot run until CW-0011 lands.
- `make lint`: same root-cause; fails at first step.
- End-of-wave grep gate (Path B aliased symbols) on every edited file: zero hits.
- Both edited files pass `gofmt -e`.

## Refs

- Sprint: SP-20260508-0001
- Parent: CW-20260508-0008
- Sibling: CW-20260508-0011 (Anthropic), CW-20260508-0012 (OpenAI), CW-20260508-0013 (slim go-providers)
- Implementer prompt: `agent-workspaces/execution/nanite/sp-20260508-0001/2026-05-09/cw-0010-cli-prune/implementer-prompt.md`
- Implementer report: `agent-workspaces/execution/nanite/sp-20260508-0001/2026-05-09/cw-0010-cli-prune/implementer-report.md`
- Wave 2 amendments: `wave2-prompt-amendments.md`
- Adjacent decision: `decisions.nanite.architecture.go_llm_contracts_split` (rev `01KR6XWJYWE7TWA1AW5DJYM717`)
- Memory: `feedback_no_compat_shims` (clean-break authority), `feedback_plan_is_best_effort` (pre-launch back-compat is zero factor)
